paragraphs: Fostering for children in Cambridge is run by Cambridgeshire County Council, which covers the city and the surrounding districts, together with independent agencies such as those shown above. The council belongs to Foster East, a group of 11 councils that share recruitment, and in December 2024 it said there were 7,000 children in care across the East of England and that Cambridgeshire was short of foster carers.

The council says its greatest needs are homes for children aged 11 and over, for brothers and sisters, and for children with complex needs and disabilities. In November 2023 it appealed to parents whose own children had left home, saying more than 400 young people aged 12 to 18 in the county could not live with their birth families.

You need to be over 21, and there is no upper age limit. Single people and couples can apply, as can renters, pet owners and people who work full or part time. After a first call and a home visit, applicants are invited to apply, take a four-day course called Journey to Foster during the assessment, and then go to the fostering panel. The council aims to finish the assessment within four months.

The council says its pay competes with independent agencies and lists extras such as Fostertalk membership, legal protection insurance and a confidential counselling line, along with a supervising social worker and a mentor in the first year. Ask the council and two or three of the agencies above what each offers before you choose. The Cambridgeshire page lists more services in the county.
